about: 38 Florida education funding streams, coded by which kinds of organization can be paid from each and how. Compiled October 2026 from the FY 2026–27 FEFP conference report, the Governor's budget highlights, Florida Statutes and agency handbooks. Ported to WMFC on 16 Oct 2026; rows marked verified were re-read against statute that day.

recodes.why: Authorized use: tuition and fees at an eligible postsecondary educational institution or its program. s. 1002.394(4)(b)4.
Authorized use: contracted services provided by a public school or school district, including classes. s. 1002.394(4)(b)7.
Same clause: charter schools are public schools, so they fall under "contracted services provided by a public school." s. 1002.394(4)(b)7.
PEP authorized use: contracted services provided by a public school or school district, including classes. s. 1002.395(6)(d)4.f.
Same clause as districts; charter schools are public schools. s. 1002.395(6)(d)4.f.

types.label: Individual or sole proprietor
types.hint: A tutor, coach, consultant or one-person business with no separate entity.

types.label: For-profit company
types.hint: An LLC, Inc, PA or similar registered with the Division of Corporations.

types.label: Nonprofit, 501(c)(3)
types.hint: A tax-exempt organization, including faith-based and community organizations.

types.label: Licensed clinical practice
types.hint: Speech, occupational, behavioral or mental health services under a Florida licence.

types.label: Licensed early learning centre
types.hint: A child care centre or preschool licensed or licence-exempt through DCF.

types.label: Private school
types.hint: A nonpublic K-12 school, including faith-based schools.

types.label: Homeschool co-op or microschool
types.hint: A parent-organized learning group or small unaccredited school.

types.label: Workforce or technical training
types.hint: A trade, CTE or credential-training provider that is not a college.

types.label: Charter school
types.hint: A public charter school authorized under s. 1002.33.

types.label: School district
types.hint: A Florida public school district or its career centre.

types.label: College or university
types.hint: A Florida College System institution, state university or private college.

streams.name: Florida Education Finance Program — district and charter share
streams.agency: FLDOE, Office of Funding and Financial Reporting
streams.per: $9,337.67 per unweighted FTE; base student allocation $5,457.60
streams.elig: Public school districts, charter schools authorised under s. 1002.33, lab schools and the Florida Virtual School. Funding follows enrolled full-time-equivalent students, weighted by programme.
streams.vendor: There is no vendor registration for the FEFP itself. Money reaches a business only through a district or charter school purchase. That means competitive solicitation under the district's purchasing rules and ch. 287 principles, a district vendor registration, W-9 and insurance certificates, and Level 2 background screening under s. 1012.32 for any personnel with direct student contact. Many districts also require fingerprinting through their own badge office rather than accepting an outside clearance.
streams.pay: District pays the vendor on its own accounts-payable cycle, typically net 30–45 after invoice and delivery acceptance. State funds reach districts on a bi-monthly distribution schedule.
streams.window: District solicitations run year-round; most instructional purchasing concentrates between February and July, before the school year starts.
streams.audit: District annual financial report to FLDOE, FTE enrolment audits by the Auditor General, retention of procurement records. Vendors are subject to whatever audit rights the district contract reserves.

streams.name: Family Empowerment Scholarship — Educational Options (FES-EO)
streams.agency: FLDOE, administered by scholarship funding organisations (Step Up For Students)
streams.per: 320,439 students. Award varies by district and grade: roughly $8,238–$12,217 in grades K–3 and $7,463–$11,421 in grades 9–12
streams.elig: Any student eligible to enrol in a Florida public school, at any income level. Priority to households at or below 185% of federal poverty when demand exceeds funds. Most of the award goes to private school tuition, with the remainder usable on approved services.
streams.vendor: Create a business account in the EMA platform operated by the scholarship funding organisation. Submit business licences, curriculum or service samples, and background screening for any staff who work with students. Staff delivering credentialed services also need individual provider accounts with credential documentation. Live classes and tutoring require a separate approval on top of any underlying credential. Link a bank account to the platform's payment processor. Private schools must separately register with FLDOE and meet the accountability requirements in s. 1002.421.
streams.pay: Three routes. Direct pay to an approved provider through the platform, with no out-of-pocket cost to the family. Purchase through the pre-approved product marketplace. Or family reimbursement, where the family pays first and files receipts.
streams.window: Applications for the following school year open in January; priority deadline 30 April. Funds disburse to accounts quarterly. Reimbursement claims must match purchases in the same 1 July–30 June year.
streams.audit: Scholarship funding organisation audits of provider invoicing and eligibility, receipt retention, and periodic re-verification of credentials. A 2026 Auditor General operational audit found significant control weaknesses, and SB 318 would have added oversight before stalling. Expect tighter documentation requirements ahead.

streams.name: Family Empowerment Scholarship — Unique Abilities (FES-UA)
streams.agency: FLDOE, administered by scholarship funding organisations
streams.per: 172,960 students. Base award roughly $10,402–$14,381 in grades K–3. Students at ESE support level IV receive roughly $21,379–$25,701 and at level V roughly $34,429–$39,091
streams.elig: Students aged 3 to 22 with a qualifying diagnosed disability. No income test. Unused funds roll over, so accounts can accumulate well beyond the annual award.
streams.vendor: Same platform onboarding as FES-EO, plus the underlying Florida professional licence for any therapeutic service. Speech-language pathology, occupational therapy and behaviour analysis all require the relevant Florida licence or board certification. The scholarship does not create a licensure shortcut. Specialists must hold both the licence and the platform approval.
streams.pay: Direct pay to approved providers, marketplace purchase, or family reimbursement. Quarterly disbursement to the account.
streams.window: Applications open January, priority deadline 30 April. Rolling for eligible new diagnoses.
streams.audit: Provider invoicing audits, credential re-verification, and documentation that services delivered match the student's needs. Same tightening oversight environment as FES-EO.

streams.name: Florida Tax Credit Scholarship, including the Personalized Education Program
streams.agency: Scholarship funding organisations under FLDOE oversight
streams.per: Roughly $8,000 average per student. PEP capacity reported at 140,000 students for 2026–27
streams.elig: FTC serves students attending eligible private schools. PEP serves K–12 students in parent-directed education who are not enrolled full-time in a public or private school and are not registered in a Florida home education programme. Open to all income levels, with priority to lower-income households.
streams.vendor: Identical platform onboarding to the Family Empowerment scholarships — the same business account, credential documentation and background screening apply. PEP is the broadest spending category for non-school businesses: curriculum, part-time tutoring, educational therapies, live online classes, enrichment, and postsecondary courses at institutions participating in the state authorisation reciprocity agreement.
streams.pay: Direct pay, marketplace, or reimbursement. Funded by tax credits against corporate income, insurance premium and several other state taxes rather than by appropriation.
streams.window: 2026–27 applications closed 30 April 2026 for both new and renewing students. The 2027–28 window is expected to open in January 2027.
streams.audit: Scholarship funding organisation reporting to FLDOE, annual norm-referenced testing for participating students, provider invoicing audits.
streams.flag: Dollar volume unconfirmed: this programme is tax-credit funded and does not appear in the FEFP appropriations report. Sources also disagree on whether the 2026–27 PEP cap is 100,000 or 140,000; the administrator's own figure is used here.

streams.name: Class Size Reduction allocation
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.authority: s. 1011.685, F.S.; Art. IX s. 1, Fla. Const.
streams.per: Allocated by district against constitutional class-size caps
streams.elig: All school districts, calculated on compliance with the constitutional maximum class size.
streams.vendor: Reaches businesses only as district operating spend — chiefly staffing. Access is through district procurement and, for staffing firms, through district-approved contract instructional personnel arrangements with the same background screening obligations.
streams.pay: State distribution to districts; vendor payment on district accounts-payable terms.
streams.window: District budget adopted in September; spending decisions largely set in the spring before.
streams.audit: Class size compliance calculation and reporting; district financial audit.

streams.name: Exceptional Student Education guaranteed allocation
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Distributed by district on prior-year ESE enrolment
streams.elig: Districts, to serve students with disabilities at support levels not otherwise funded through weighted FTE.
streams.vendor: Districts contract out related services — therapy, assistive technology, specialised assessment, interpreters — when in-house capacity is short. Requires the underlying Florida professional licence, district vendor registration, and Level 2 screening. This is one of the few categoricals with a genuine external services market.
streams.pay: District contract, paid on district terms; often per-session or per-evaluation rates set in the contract.
streams.window: District related-services contracts are typically solicited in spring for the following school year, with mid-year additions when caseloads exceed capacity.
streams.audit: Service logs tied to individual education plans, Medicaid certification where services are billed through school-based Medicaid, district financial audit.

streams.name: Teacher Salary Increase allocation
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Raises capped at $3,000 for eligible teachers with ten or more years of experience
streams.elig: Districts and charter schools, restricted to salary increases for full-time classroom teachers and certified prekindergarten teachers funded through the FEFP.
streams.vendor: Not accessible to outside providers. Listed because it is a large share of the FEFP and is frequently mistaken for discretionary district money.
streams.pay: Distributed to districts within the FEFP; restricted use.
streams.window: Annual; allocation plans filed with FLDOE.
streams.audit: District salary allocation plan and compliance reporting to FLDOE.

streams.name: Educational Enrichment allocation
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Distributed by district
streams.elig: Districts, for supplemental academic instruction and enrichment consistent with the allocation's statutory purposes.
streams.vendor: Districts purchase tutoring, intervention curricula and supplemental programmes from this allocation. Evidence-of-effectiveness documentation is commonly requested. Standard district vendor registration and screening apply.
streams.pay: District contract or purchase order.
streams.window: Spring purchasing for the following year; mid-year intervention buys after winter progress monitoring.
streams.audit: District expenditure reporting against allocation purposes.

streams.name: Academic Acceleration Options supplement
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Distributed on qualifying accelerated course and industry certification outcomes
streams.elig: Districts, based on student performance in advanced placement, international baccalaureate, dual enrollment, advanced international certificate of education and industry certification.
streams.vendor: Certification bodies and exam vendors are paid here, as are curriculum and test-preparation providers. Industry certifications must appear on the state's funding-eligible certification list, which is itself an application process for a certifying body.
streams.pay: Performance-based distribution to districts, which then purchase.
streams.window: Certification list submissions run on an annual FLDOE cycle; district purchasing in spring and summer.
streams.audit: Outcome verification against certification and exam records.

streams.name: Student Transportation allocation
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Distributed by district on eligible ridership
streams.elig: Districts, for transporting eligible students.
streams.vendor: Contracted transportation is a real market. Requires commercial vehicle compliance, driver qualification and screening under s. 1012.45, insurance at district-specified limits, and a competitive solicitation win.
streams.pay: District contract, usually per-route or per-day rates.
streams.window: Multi-year contracts solicited well ahead of the school year.
streams.audit: Ridership and route documentation, driver qualification files, vehicle inspection records.

streams.name: Safe Schools allocation
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Distributed by district
streams.elig: Districts, for school resource officers, guardians, safety technology and threat assessment.
streams.vendor: Security technology, threat assessment platforms, panic alert systems and training providers sell into this allocation. Products must meet FLDOE specifications where they exist, and panic alert systems must interoperate with the statewide requirements.
streams.pay: District contract or purchase order.
streams.window: Summer procurement ahead of the school year is typical.
streams.audit: District safety compliance reporting and the Florida Safe Schools Assessment Tool.

streams.name: Mental Health Assistance allocation
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Distributed by district
streams.elig: Districts, for mental health assessment, intervention and referral services for students.
streams.vendor: Districts contract licensed clinicians and community behavioural health agencies. Requires the Florida clinical licence, district vendor registration, Level 2 screening, and often a memorandum of understanding rather than a purchase order.
streams.pay: District contract, commonly per-service or staffed-position rates.
streams.window: District mental health plans are filed annually with FLDOE, usually mid-year, and drive the next year's contracting.
streams.audit: District mental health assistance plan and outcome reporting to FLDOE; clinical documentation standards.

streams.name: Charter school capital outlay
streams.agency: FLDOE, Office of Fixed Capital Outlay
streams.per: Per-pupil facilities allocation, weighted 1.25× or 1.5× for schools with high free-and-reduced-lunch or disability enrolment
streams.elig: Charter schools meeting one of several qualifying criteria — three years of operation, governance by an established board operating multiple charter schools, an expanded feeder chain, regional accreditation, or charter-school-in-the-workplace status — plus a clean audit, satisfactory student achievement, sponsor approval, and occupancy of a facility not provided by the sponsor.
streams.vendor: Reaches construction, maintenance, renovation and facilities-finance businesses through the charter school's own procurement, which is generally less restrictive than a district's.
streams.pay: State distribution to eligible charter schools; the school pays vendors directly. Funded from the capital outlay trust fund and discretionary millage revenue.
streams.window: Charter school capital outlay plans are due to FLDOE by 1 July, with sponsoring district review by 1 August.
streams.audit: Annual audit free of financial emergency conditions, capital outlay plan compliance, facility eligibility verification.

streams.name: Hope Scholarship
streams.agency: FLDOE, administered by scholarship funding organisations
streams.per: Award tracks the private school scholarship amount
streams.elig: Public school students who report an incident of battery, harassment, hazing, bullying, threat, robbery, sexual offence, fighting or similar. Eligibility is triggered by the reported incident, not by income.
streams.vendor: Same scholarship platform onboarding as the other programmes. Private schools must be registered and compliant with s. 1002.421.
streams.pay: Direct pay or reimbursement, funded by voluntary contributions from motor vehicle purchasers in exchange for a sales tax credit.
streams.window: Year-round. Applications follow the incident report rather than an annual cycle, which makes this the only mid-year entry point among the scholarships.
streams.audit: Incident documentation, scholarship funding organisation reporting.
streams.flag: Dollar volume unconfirmed. Funded by tax credits rather than appropriation.

streams.name: New Worlds Scholarship Accounts
streams.agency: FLDOE, administered by scholarship funding organisations
streams.per: Historically around $1,200 per student
streams.elig: Public school students in kindergarten through grade 5 identified with a substantial deficiency in reading, and separately students with mathematics deficiencies.
streams.vendor: Narrow spending categories — instructional materials, tutoring, curriculum and summer or after-school literacy and numeracy programmes — through the same scholarship platform. The narrowness is the constraint, not the approval.
streams.pay: Marketplace purchase or reimbursement.
streams.window: Applications typically open in spring following progress monitoring identification.
streams.audit: Scholarship funding organisation reporting; expenditures must fall inside the restricted category list.
streams.flag: Current-year appropriation and award amount unconfirmed.

streams.name: School hardening and nonpublic school security grants
streams.agency: FLDOE / Florida Department of Law Enforcement
streams.per: $20M public school hardening; $20M security at Jewish day schools and preschools
streams.elig: Public schools for the hardening grant. Jewish day schools and preschools for the dedicated security grant, which is one of the few state streams that pays into nonpublic settings directly.
streams.vendor: Physical security contractors, access control and camera integrators, and security staffing firms are the vendors. Grant recipients procure; requirements are set by the recipient school rather than a state vendor list.
streams.pay: Grant to the school, which then contracts.
streams.window: Grant application cycles announced by the administering agency, typically summer.
streams.audit: Grant expenditure reporting and, for the public school hardening grant, safety assessment compliance.
streams.flag: The Governor's budget highlights lists the Jewish day school security amount as $20 million in its K–12 section and $9 million in its public safety section. The higher figure is shown; the discrepancy is unresolved.

streams.name: Voluntary Prekindergarten
streams.agency: FLDOE Division of Early Learning, delivered by regional early learning coalitions
streams.per: $3,029 per child for the school-year programme, $2,586 for summer. Roughly 136,000 children served
streams.elig: Every child who turns four by 1 September, regardless of family income, under the 2002 constitutional amendment. Families choose a private centre or a public school programme.
streams.vendor: Sign a VPK provider agreement with your regional early learning coalition. You need a Department of Children and Families child care licence or a documented exemption, Level 2 background screening for all staff, a lead instructor holding a VPK director credential or equivalent qualification, completion of the required emergent literacy training sequence, and participation in coordinated screening and progress monitoring plus the classroom quality assessment.
streams.pay: Monthly payment from the coalition against certified attendance. Payment follows the child to the provider, which makes this the closest thing in early learning to a portable-funding model.
streams.window: Provider agreements renew annually before the school year. Child enrolment is rolling, with a summer programme for children who missed the school-year option.
streams.audit: Attendance certification, coalition monitoring visits, programme assessment scores and kindergarten readiness results. Low-performing providers face improvement plans and can lose eligibility.

streams.name: School Readiness
streams.agency: FLDOE Division of Early Learning, delivered by regional early learning coalitions
streams.authority: ss. 1002.81–1002.92, F.S.; federal Child Care and Development Fund
streams.per: Reimbursement rates set regionally by each coalition, with quality differentials
streams.elig: Children from birth to school entry in low-income working families, plus children in protective services and other priority categories. Most funding comes from the federal Child Care and Development Block Grant rather than state revenue.
streams.vendor: School Readiness provider agreement with the coalition. Requires a Department of Children and Families licence or license-exempt registration, background screening, health and safety training, and participation in the programme assessment and quality rating system. Gold Seal quality accreditation raises your reimbursement rate, which is the single highest-leverage improvement available to a provider in this stream.
streams.pay: Monthly reimbursement from the coalition at the regional rate, based on certified attendance. Family co-payments are collected by the provider.
streams.window: Provider agreements renew annually. Family eligibility is determined by the coalition, with waiting lists in most regions.
streams.audit: Attendance records, coalition monitoring and fraud investigation, quality assessment scores, health and safety inspection.

streams.name: Early learning quality and workforce initiatives
streams.agency: FLDOE Division of Early Learning
streams.authority: General Appropriations Act; federal CCDBG quality set-aside
streams.per: $20M teacher scholarships, $6.5M developmental screening and referral, $3.9M home-based preschool curriculum delivery, $3.5M instructional quality
streams.elig: Varies by initiative. The teacher scholarship programme funds credential attainment for working early childhood educators. The home instruction programme delivers curriculum to parents of at-risk preschoolers.
streams.vendor: Several of these are operated by a designated statewide intermediary rather than open to any vendor. Curriculum publishers, training providers and coaching organisations reach the money as subcontractors to that intermediary or to individual coalitions.
streams.pay: Grant or contract through the administering intermediary or a coalition.
streams.window: Follows the state fiscal year beginning 1 July.
streams.audit: Grant expenditure and outcome reporting.

streams.name: Head Start and Early Head Start
streams.agency: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families
streams.per: Awarded per funded enrolment slot; Florida total not confirmed
streams.elig: Children from birth to five in families at or below the federal poverty line, plus categorical eligibility for children in foster care, experiencing homelessness, or receiving public assistance.
streams.vendor: Head Start money is awarded federally, direct to grantees, bypassing the state entirely. Becoming a grantee or delegate agency means winning a federal competition and then meeting the Head Start Program Performance Standards, including staff degree requirements, comprehensive services, and a governing body plus policy council structure. Existing grantees do subcontract for specialised services, which is the realistic entry point.
streams.pay: Federal grant draw-down against an approved budget.
streams.window: Competitions announced by the federal office; recompetition is triggered by designation renewal findings rather than a fixed schedule.
streams.audit: Federal monitoring reviews, single audit under 2 CFR 200, performance standards compliance.
streams.flag: No Florida total confirmed. The programme also faced proposed federal reductions during the FY 2026 appropriations cycle.

streams.name: Title I, Part A — improving basic programs
streams.agency: U.S. Department of Education, passed through FLDOE to districts
streams.authority: Elementary and Secondary Education Act, Title I Part A
streams.per: Formula allocation on poverty counts; Florida total not confirmed
streams.elig: Districts and schools serving concentrations of students from low-income families. The state reserves a portion for school improvement and administration before subgranting.
streams.vendor: Reached only through district purchasing. The practical differentiator is evidence: districts buying with Title I funds are expected to select interventions meeting the evidence tiers defined in the Act, so a provider without study documentation is at a structural disadvantage regardless of product quality.
streams.pay: District contract or purchase order, on district accounts-payable terms.
streams.window: District Title I plans are set in spring for the following year. Federal awards themselves arrive in two instalments, in July and October.
streams.audit: Supplement-not-supplant testing, single audit under 2 CFR 200, evidence and allowability documentation.
streams.flag: Florida allocation unconfirmed. Federal FY 2026 Title I awards were split across July and October payments with revised final allocations issued in September, so figures published earlier are provisional.

streams.name: IDEA Part B and Part C
streams.agency: U.S. Department of Education and HHS, passed through FLDOE and the early steps system
streams.per: Formula allocation; Florida total not confirmed
streams.elig: Part B serves children aged three to 21 with disabilities through the schools. Part C serves infants and toddlers from birth to three through the state early intervention system.
streams.vendor: Part B reaches providers as contracted related services through districts. Part C is the more accessible half: the state early intervention system enrols independent licensed providers to deliver services in natural environments, which for a small clinical practice is a genuine open door.
streams.pay: District contract for Part B. Part C providers bill the early intervention system at established rates.
streams.window: Part B contracting follows the school year. Part C provider enrolment is rolling.
streams.audit: Service documentation against individual education or family service plans, single audit, state monitoring.

streams.name: Title II-A, Title III and Title IV-A
streams.agency: U.S. Department of Education, passed through FLDOE to districts
streams.per: Formula allocations; Florida totals not confirmed
streams.elig: Title II-A funds educator preparation and professional development. Title III funds language instruction for English learners and immigrant students. Title IV-A funds well-rounded education, safe and healthy students, and educational technology.
streams.vendor: These are the federal streams most open to professional development providers, language-instruction curriculum publishers and enrichment programmes — Title IV-A in particular has broad allowable uses. Access is still through district procurement, but the buying criteria are less rigid than Title I's.
streams.pay: District contract or purchase order.
streams.window: District consolidated federal grant applications are filed in spring for the following year.
streams.audit: Allowability documentation, supplement-not-supplant where applicable, single audit.

streams.name: Perkins V career and technical education basic state grant
streams.agency: U.S. Department of Education, passed through FLDOE to districts and colleges
streams.authority: Carl D. Perkins Career and Technical Education Act, as amended by Perkins V
streams.per: Roughly $1.4B appropriated nationally; Florida share not confirmed
streams.elig: Secondary and postsecondary CTE programmes. States pass at least 85% through to local recipients on a population and poverty formula.
streams.vendor: Every local recipient must complete a comprehensive local needs assessment tying spending to labour market data and student performance, and those applications are generally public. Reading them tells you exactly what each district and college plans to buy and why — the most underused piece of market intelligence in Florida CTE. Equipment, industry certification, work-based learning platforms and instructor training all sell into this.
streams.pay: Local recipient contract or purchase order.
streams.window: Local applications are filed annually with FLDOE, typically in spring.
streams.audit: Needs assessment alignment, performance indicator reporting disaggregated by special population, single audit.

streams.name: Career and Technical Education operational funding
streams.agency: FLDOE Division of Career and Adult Education
streams.per: Operational funding across district career centres and college CTE programmes
streams.elig: District postsecondary technical career centres, charter technical career centres and Florida College System institutions delivering CTE programmes.
streams.vendor: Equipment, simulation, curriculum, certification and instructor-training vendors sell into institutional procurement. Programmes themselves must appear on the state CTE programme inventory, which is an FLDOE approval process for the institution rather than the vendor.
streams.pay: Institutional contract or purchase order.
streams.window: Institutional budgets set for the fiscal year beginning 1 July; equipment purchasing often concentrates late in the fiscal year.
streams.audit: Programme enrolment and completion reporting, placement outcomes through the state education and training placement data system.

streams.name: Workforce Development Capitalization Incentive Grant
streams.agency: FLDOE Division of Career and Adult Education
streams.per: Competitive awards for creating or expanding CTE programmes
streams.elig: Institutions proposing to start or expand programmes that respond to a documented local workforce need, typically with employer commitment evidence.
streams.vendor: The grant funds equipment and start-up costs, so equipment suppliers and curriculum partners are the beneficiaries. The stronger play is partnering on the application itself: an employer or industry partner named in a proposal shapes what gets bought.
streams.pay: Competitive grant to the institution, which then procures.
streams.window: Annual competitive cycle announced by FLDOE.
streams.audit: Grant performance reporting on enrolment, completion and placement.

streams.name: Pathways to Career Opportunities Grant
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: Includes $5M dedicated to a teacher registered apprenticeship programme
streams.elig: Programmes establishing or expanding registered pre-apprenticeship and apprenticeship opportunities for high school and college students.
streams.vendor: A business can be a registered apprenticeship sponsor in its own right. That means registering the programme with the state apprenticeship office, documenting the work process schedule and related technical instruction, and meeting apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio and wage progression requirements. Sponsorship is the access route — this is one of the few workforce streams where the employer is the grantee.
streams.pay: Grant to the sponsor or the partnering institution.
streams.window: Annual grant cycle. Apprenticeship programme registration itself is rolling but takes months.
streams.audit: Apprentice registration records, completion and retention reporting, wage progression compliance.
streams.flag: Appropriation confirmed. Authorising statute section not confirmed and deliberately left blank rather than guessed.

streams.name: Open Door Grant Program
streams.agency: FLDOE Office of Student Financial Assistance
streams.authority: s. 1009.895, F.S.; Fla. Admin. Code R. 6A-20.045
streams.per: Covers 100% of tuition, fees, exam costs, books and materials after other aid, plus a stipend of up to $1,500 per academic year
streams.elig: Students enrolling in short-term, high-demand credit and non-credit CTE programmes.
streams.vendor: This is the trap in the workforce portfolio. An eligible institution is defined narrowly as a school district postsecondary technical career centre under s. 1001.44, a Florida College System institution, or a charter technical career centre under s. 1002.34. A private training company cannot receive Open Door funds no matter how in-demand its programme is. The realistic routes are contracting to deliver a programme for an eligible institution, or chartering a technical career centre.
streams.pay: Allocation to the eligible institution, which awards students and applies funds to their cost of attendance.
streams.window: Institutional allocations set annually. Each institution receives a base of at least 90% of its prior-year disbursements, with the remainder distributed proportionally on three-year student counts — which locks in incumbents.
streams.audit: Disbursement and student eligibility reporting to the Office of Student Financial Assistance.

streams.name: WIOA Title I — adult, dislocated worker and youth training
streams.agency: FloridaCommerce and CareerSource Florida, delivered by regional workforce boards
streams.authority: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, Title I
streams.per: Individual training accounts sized by the local board; Florida allocation not confirmed
streams.elig: Adults and dislocated workers meeting income and employment criteria, plus eligible youth. Participants choose from the approved provider list, which is what makes this an open market.
streams.vendor: Apply through the statewide training provider portal in the state labour exchange system. You must be licensed, certified or otherwise authorised under Florida law to provide training; your programme must lead to a recognised postsecondary credential and appear on a statewide or regional demand occupations list; the occupation's entry wage generally must meet or exceed the region's lower living standard income level; and you must agree to supply student outcome data to the state placement information programme annually. Initial eligibility runs one year, then continued eligibility every two years. Registered apprenticeship sponsors are exempt from the application requirements.
streams.pay: The local board pays the provider directly against an individual training account for an enrolled participant. Listing does not guarantee referrals — participants and career coaches choose.
streams.window: Applications open through the state portal, but several regional boards accept new providers only in the first quarter of the programme year, after the regional demand occupations list publishes.
streams.audit: Annual outcome data submission, performance against employment and earnings measures, continued eligibility review, single audit at the board level.

streams.name: Florida Job Growth Grant Fund
streams.agency: FloridaCommerce, at the Governor's approval
streams.per: Project-based awards for public infrastructure and workforce training
streams.elig: Public infrastructure projects and workforce training programmes at state colleges, career centres and similar institutions. Proposals come from local governments and institutions, not private firms.
streams.vendor: Training curriculum and equipment vendors are paid by the awarded institution. The lever is employer demand: proposals are strengthened by documented commitments from employers who will hire the trainees, which is a role a business can play without being the applicant.
streams.pay: Grant to the applicant, which then procures.
streams.window: Rolling proposals, reviewed and approved by the Governor's office.
streams.audit: Grant agreement performance milestones and expenditure reporting.

streams.name: Industry certification and student success performance funding
streams.agency: FLDOE
streams.per: $8.5M for certifications at career technical centres, $20M at Florida colleges, $30M through the 2+2 and Work Florida student success incentive funds
streams.elig: Institutions earn this on student attainment of industry certifications in high-skill, high-demand areas and on transfer and completion outcomes.
streams.vendor: Certifying bodies and exam providers are the direct beneficiaries. Getting a credential onto the state's funding-eligible certification list is the single decision that determines whether institutions will push students toward it — and that list is an annual FLDOE submission process open to certification providers.
streams.pay: Performance distribution to institutions, which purchase exams and preparation.
streams.window: Annual certification list submission cycle; institutional purchasing follows.
streams.audit: Certification attainment verification against the funding list.

streams.name: Nursing education incentive funds — PIPELINE and LINE
streams.agency: FLDOE and the Board of Governors
streams.per: $100M rewarding nursing programme performance, $30M incentivising education and healthcare partnerships
streams.elig: Approved nursing education programmes at Florida institutions, measured on completion and licensure exam pass rates. The partnership fund requires a healthcare employer partner.
streams.vendor: Simulation equipment, clinical placement management software and exam preparation vendors sell here. Healthcare employers are named partners in the second fund, which is a direct participation route for a provider organisation.
streams.pay: Performance distribution to institutions and matched partnership awards.
streams.window: Annual, tied to the fiscal year and programme outcome reporting.
streams.audit: Completion and licensure pass rate verification; partnership match documentation.

streams.name: Dual enrollment
streams.agency: FLDOE, districts and postsecondary institutions
streams.per: Districts reimburse postsecondary institutions for instruction; a separate state scholarship covers private school and home education students
streams.elig: Secondary students, including private school and home education students, meeting the institution's readiness requirements. Students pay no tuition, fees or instructional materials costs.
streams.vendor: Instructional materials for dual enrollment courses are a defined cost that someone must bear, and the statute allocates that responsibility. Course delivery itself requires being an eligible postsecondary institution with faculty meeting accreditation credential standards, which is not reachable by a new entrant.
streams.pay: District payment to the institution, or state scholarship payment for non-district students.
streams.window: Articulation agreements between districts and institutions are updated annually, typically by spring.
streams.audit: Enrolment and course completion reporting; articulation agreement compliance.
streams.flag: Current-year appropriation for the dual enrollment scholarship unconfirmed.

streams.name: Bright Futures Scholarship Program
streams.agency: FLDOE Office of Student Financial Assistance
streams.per: Award levels set by scholarship tier and institution type
streams.elig: Florida high school graduates meeting the academic, testing and service hour requirements for the relevant award tier.
streams.vendor: Only eligible Florida postsecondary institutions receive these funds. For a K–12 business the reachable adjacency is upstream: test preparation, service hour tracking, and eligibility advising sold to families or districts — none of which is itself Bright Futures money.
streams.pay: Disbursed to the institution and applied to the student's account.
streams.window: Applications filed by high school graduation; disbursement each term.
streams.audit: Institutional disbursement reporting and student eligibility verification.

streams.name: Florida College System and State University System operating funds
streams.agency: FLDOE and the Board of Governors
streams.per: $1.8B state colleges, $3.9B universities. A further $645M in university performance funding
streams.elig: Florida College System institutions and State University System universities.
streams.vendor: Institutional procurement under ch. 287 principles and each institution's own purchasing regulations. Cooperative purchasing agreements and state term contracts are the shortest path for a vendor already on one — getting onto a state term contract removes the need to win each institution separately.
streams.pay: Institutional contract or purchase order.
streams.window: Fiscal year beginning 1 July; solicitations run year-round.
streams.audit: Institutional financial audit; Auditor General operational audits.

streams.name: Required local effort property tax
streams.agency: County property appraisers and school district tax collection
streams.per: 3.057 mills statewide for 2026–27
streams.elig: Levied by every district as the local share of the FEFP. It is counted inside the $30.03B FEFP total, not on top of it.
streams.vendor: No separate access route. Included so the FEFP total is not misread as state money.
streams.pay: Property tax collection, credited against the district's FEFP entitlement.
streams.window: Annual millage certification with the tax roll.
streams.audit: Tax roll certification and district financial audit.

streams.name: Discretionary local effort and local capital millage
streams.agency: School districts
streams.per: 0.748 discretionary mills. A separate local capital improvement millage of up to 1.5 mills is authorised and not included in this figure
streams.elig: Districts levying the discretionary operating millage, plus the separate capital improvement millage which funds construction, maintenance, equipment and certain leases — and which also feeds charter school capital outlay.
streams.vendor: The capital millage is where district construction, renovation, technology infrastructure and equipment money sits. Access is competitive solicitation, with continuing services contracts for design professionals under s. 287.055 offering a longer-lived vehicle than one-off bids.
streams.pay: District contract, often with progress payments and retainage for construction.
streams.window: Capital plans adopted annually with a five-year work programme, which is public and shows what is coming.
streams.audit: Capital expenditure restrictions under s. 1011.71(2), district financial audit, plant survey compliance.
streams.flag: The 1.5-mill capital improvement millage total was not calculated and is not included in the figure shown.

streams.name: District education foundations and private philanthropy
streams.agency: Local direct-support organisations; FLDOE administers a state match
streams.per: State matching grant amounts vary by year and by foundation fundraising
streams.elig: Direct-support organisations chartered to support a school district, which raise private funds and may qualify for a state match on eligible programmes.
streams.vendor: Foundations fund classroom grants, teacher supply programmes, scholarships and innovation pilots. They are far faster to contract with than their districts, do not follow public procurement rules, and are the most common route for a pilot that later becomes a district purchase. Approach the foundation, not the purchasing department, when you need a first reference customer.
streams.pay: Grant or direct purchase by the foundation.
streams.window: Most foundations run classroom grant cycles in autumn and spring.
streams.audit: Foundation audit and reporting to the district; state matching grant reporting where applicable.
streams.flag: No statewide total confirmed. Matching grant availability varies by year.
